Definition: Kedar, a son of Ishmael; also (collectively) Bedouin (as his descendants or representatives)
BiblicalUsage: Kedar is the son of Ishmael and the people of the desert tents: these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, Nebajoth, and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam; within a year, and all the glory of Kedar shall fail. The psalmist cries, woe is me, that I dwell in the tents of Kedar.
TheologicalSignificance: I take the tents of Kedar as the picture of a life far from home, and the failing glory as the end of every people that trusts in itself.
